assumptions: Technical failures are those with failure category 'technical'; failure rate is each bank's technical failures as a share of its own attempts.
caveats: The hourly timeline and the day-level view cover only a sample of the data shown, so the exact start and end hour of the 17-18 September incident should be confirmed from the full timeline.
The data-quality scan found no issues for September.

facts.text: Kestrel Bank had 2,776 technical failed attempts in September 2026, 33.4% of the 8,322 technical failures across acquirers. That is a technical failure rate of 2.94% of its 94,315 attempts.

The next highest were Meridian Bank (1,965 failures, 2.14% of its attempts), Northstar Bank (1,806, 2.20%) and Saffron Bank (1,775, 2.09%). The top three banks together account for 78.7% of technical failures.
Kestrel's daily success rate was mostly steady around 89-90% in the first half of September. Anomaly detection flagged two drop windows: 4 September and 17-18 September.

Comparing 17-18 September with 10-16 September, success rates fell sharply for debit cards (30.11pp, from 86.42% to 56.31%), credit cards (28.71pp, from 88.64% to 59.94%) and card EMI (23.87pp, from 80.67% to 56.80%). UPI, wallet and netbanking did not change significantly.
Over the same comparison, the ACQ_TIMEOUT failure code rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts on Kestrel's card methods, from 22 to 803 failures. Other failure codes did not rise materially.

response.headline: Kestrel Bank had the most technical payment failures in September, with 2,776 failures (33.4% of all 8,322), and they clustered on 17-18 September, when card payments at Kestrel collapsed because of acquirer timeouts.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Review the hourly timeline for the exact start and end of the incident, and check Kestrel's incident or maintenance logs and latency metrics for 17-18 September.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is confined to card methods at one acquirer, and ACQ_TIMEOUT jumped from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts while other failure codes stayed flat or fell.
hypotheses.text: A timeout problem on Kestrel Bank's card processing path on 17-18 September drove most of its technical failures.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Run the same payment-method and failure-code breakdown for 4 September.
hypotheses.rationale: The daily rate fell to 88.53% that day and was flagged as an anomaly, but the evidence does not break it down by method or failure code.
hypotheses.text: The smaller dip on 4 September may be a separate, milder incident at Kestrel.

recommendations.rationale: This is where the failures concentrated and the failure code points to the acquirer side.
recommendations.text: Raise the 17-18 September ACQ_TIMEOUT spike with Kestrel Bank and ask for a root-cause analysis covering debit, credit and EMI card traffic.

recommendations.text: Set up an alert on Kestrel's ACQ_TIMEOUT rate per 100 attempts for card methods, and consider routing card traffic to other acquirers during similar episodes.
